content: Endothelial cell-specific molecule 1 (ESM-1) is a protein encoded by the ESM1 gene in humans. This gene produces a secreted protein that is predominantly expressed in endothelial cells located in lung and kidney tissues. The expression of the ESM1 gene is regulated by cytokines, indicating its potential involvement in pathological disorders that are dependent on endothelial function. The transcript of the ESM1 gene contains multiple polyadenylation signals and mRNA instability elements. The protein product of the ESM1 gene has been referred to as endocan since 2001, when Bechard and colleagues characterized it as a dermatan sulfate proteoglycan. Recent studies have identified endocan/ESM-1 as a specific biomarker for tip cells during the process of neovascularization, as demonstrated by independent research groups. The expression of endocan has been shown to increase in response to pro-angiogenic growth factors, such as vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF-2). In hypervascularized cancers, overexpression of endocan has been detected through immunohistochemical analysis using monoclonal antibodies targeting endocan/ESM-1.
